en.name: Aioli, homemade
en.summary: Homemade aioli is a garlic emulsion, usually built on raw egg yolk and oil, with none of the acidity or preservatives of a commercial jar. It belongs in the fridge from the moment it is made and should be used within 3–4 days. It does not freeze.
en.pantry: Aioli is a perishable raw-egg sauce and must not be kept at room temperature. Follow the two-hour rule — one hour if the room is above 32 °C (90 °F) — and that clock covers time on the table as well as time on the worktop while you cook. Raw garlic sitting in oil at room temperature is its own hazard: low-acid plant material held under oil at room temperature carries a botulism risk, which is another reason this sauce lives in the fridge.
en.fridge: Make it, scrape it into a clean sealed container, and get it to 4 °C (40 °F) or below straight away, on an inside shelf rather than in the door. Use it within 3–4 days. Use a clean spoon each time — dipping a used one, or a vegetable, reintroduces bacteria into a sauce that has nothing to fight them with. If you are serving it at a party, bring out a small bowl at a time and keep the rest cold.
en.freezer: Do not freeze homemade aioli. There is no freezer timeline for it, and the emulsion breaks on thawing into a pool of oil with curds of yolk in it — unfixable, and unappealing. Aioli takes only minutes to make, so make it in the amount you will use. If you have made too much, stir the surplus into a potato salad or a sandwich filling rather than trying to store it.
spoilage: The emulsion separated, with oil pooling on top
A sharp, sour or fermented smell instead of garlic and clean oil
Any specks of mould, or a discoloured skin on the surface
A grey or darkened colour, or a fizzy taste
tips: Make small batches — a few days is the whole life of this sauce.
Use the freshest eggs you can and keep everything cold while you work.
Write the date on the container lid.
Never top up an old batch with a new one; start a clean container.

faq.q: How long does homemade aioli last in the fridge?
faq.a: 3–4 days at 4 °C (40 °F) or below in a sealed container. It has no preservatives and usually contains raw egg.
No. There is no freezer timeline, and the emulsion splits on thawing into oil and curdled yolk.

faq.q: Can aioli be left out on the table?
faq.a: Only briefly. Two hours total at room temperature, one hour above 32 °C. Serve small amounts and keep the rest refrigerated.

faq.q: Is homemade aioli safe with raw egg?
faq.a: Keep it cold, make it fresh and finish it quickly. Pasteurised eggs are the safer choice, especially for anyone who is pregnant, elderly or unwell.

zh.name: 自製蒜味蛋黃醬
zh.summary: 自製 aioli 是用生蛋黃和油打出來的蒜味乳化醬，沒有市售罐裝那樣的酸度，也沒有防腐劑。從做好的那一刻起就該放冰箱，並在 3～4 天內用完。它不適合冷凍。
zh.pantry: 這是含生蛋的易腐醬料，絕對不能放在室溫。請遵守兩小時原則（室溫超過 32 °C 時為一小時），而且這個時鐘不只算上桌的時間，做菜時擱在流理台上的時間也要算。生蒜泡在油裡放室溫本身也是風險：低酸性的植物材料在室溫下浸在油中，會有肉毒桿菌的疑慮，這也是這款醬必須進冰箱的另一個理由。
zh.fridge: 打好之後刮進乾淨的密封容器，馬上放進 4 °C 以下的冰箱內側層架，不要放門邊，並在 3～4 天內用完。每次都要用乾淨的湯匙——把用過的湯匙或蔬菜直接沾下去，等於把細菌送進一個毫無防禦力的醬裡。聚餐時請每次只端出一小碗，其餘的繼續冰著。
zh.freezer: 自製 aioli 請不要冷凍。它沒有冷凍期限，而且解凍時乳化會整個破掉，變成一灘油加上凝結的蛋黃屑，救不回來也不好看。這款醬幾分鐘就能做好，所以做多少就用多少。真的做太多，不如拌進馬鈴薯沙拉或三明治內餡，而不是想辦法保存。
spoilage: 乳化分離，表面浮出一層油
聞起來刺鼻、發酸或有發酵味，而不是蒜香加乾淨的油味
出現霉點，或表面結了一層變色的膜
顏色發灰、變暗，或吃起來有氣泡感
tips: 少量製作——這款醬的壽命本來就只有幾天。
用最新鮮的蛋，製作全程保持低溫。
不要把新做的加進舊的裡續用，請換乾淨容器重做。

faq.q: 自製蒜味蛋黃醬放冰箱可以放多久？
faq.a: 密封後在 4 °C 以下冷藏 3～4 天。它沒有防腐劑，通常又含生蛋。

faq.q: 蒜味蛋黃醬可以冷凍嗎？
faq.a: 不行。沒有冷凍期限，而且解凍後乳化會破掉，分離成油和凝結的蛋黃。

faq.q: 蒜味蛋黃醬可以一直放在餐桌上嗎？
faq.a: 只能短時間。室溫累計兩小時，超過 32 °C 時一小時。請少量分次端出，其餘冷藏。

faq.q: 用生蛋做的 aioli 安全嗎？
faq.a: 保持低溫、現做現吃、盡快用完。使用殺菌蛋更保險，孕婦、長者和身體不適的人尤其建議。
